rules.title: AWS access key ID
rules.fix: Rotate the key in IAM immediately, move to instance roles or a secret manager, then purge it from git history.

rules.title: AWS secret access key
rules.fix: Rotate immediately. Never store AWS secrets in code — use IAM roles or AWS Secrets Manager.

rules.title: Private key block (RSA/EC/OPENSSH/PGP)
rules.fix: Revoke and reissue the key pair. Store private keys in a KMS/HSM or the platform keystore, never in the repo.

rules.title: GitHub token
rules.fix: Revoke the token on GitHub now (it grants repo and possibly org access), then issue a fine-grained replacement stored in CI secrets.

rules.title: Slack token or webhook URL
rules.fix: Revoke the token / regenerate the webhook, then load it from the environment.

rules.title: Stripe API key
rules.fix: Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard. A live secret key can move money — treat exposure as an incident.

rules.title: Google API key or OAuth client secret
rules.fix: Rotate in Google Cloud Console and apply API key restrictions (referrer/IP/API scope).

rules.title: OpenAI / Anthropic / model provider API key
rules.fix: Revoke the key with the provider. Model keys are billed per token — exposure is both a data and a cost incident.

rules.title: Database connection string with inline password
rules.fix: Rotate the database password, move the DSN to the environment, and restrict the DB user to the minimum privileges.

rules.title: JSON Web Token committed in source
rules.fix: If the token is live, invalidate the session and rotate the signing key. Never commit real tokens, even expired ones.

rules.title: Telegram bot token
rules.fix: Revoke with BotFather (/revoke) and load the new token from the environment.

rules.title: Generic bearer/authorization header hardcoded
rules.fix: Build the header from a runtime secret; never literal-encode credentials in source.

rules.title: Twilio / SendGrid / Mailgun credential
rules.fix: Rotate with the provider; messaging credentials are abused for spam and phishing within minutes of exposure.

rules.title: Basic-auth credentials embedded in a URL
rules.fix: Credentials in URLs leak into logs, proxies and Referer headers. Use an Authorization header sourced from the environment.

rules.title: NPM / PyPI publish token
rules.fix: Revoke now — a publish token lets an attacker ship a malicious release to every consumer of your package.
